# pmox

> A single static Go binary that launches and manages ephemeral VMs
> on a remote Proxmox VE cluster via the PVE HTTP API. A
> multipass-style CLI for homelabs and dev clusters where Terraform
> is too much and the web UI is too slow. Does not run on the
> Proxmox host.

## Commands

`pmox init` on an already-configured machine asks: edit a server (`config edit`), add one (`context add`), or remove one (`context delete`) — it never re-asks the URL. `pmox launch` on a terminal with no default template first offers the cluster's templates or builds one (saved as the default) before asking name/size. Bare `pmox` opens a framed, filterable command palette (sections, groups open in place, Esc back).

Command structure: `pmox <noun> <verb>` — nouns `vm` (launch, clone, list|ls, info, start, stop, delete|rm, shell, exec, cp, sync, apply, ssh-config), `template` (create, list), `context`, `config`, `mount` (create, list, delete), `key`, `access`; root commands `init`, `doctor`, `cleanup`, `version`. Daily shortcuts at the root are the same commands: `launch`, `shell`, `list|ls`, `info`, `start`, `stop`, `delete|rm`, `exec`, `cp`, `sync`, `apply`, `mount`, `umount`. Old forms (`create-template`, `config *-context`, `init --list|--remove|--regen-cloud-init`, top-level `ssh-config`/`clone`) still work with a stderr deprecation note. A bare noun opens its verb picker on a terminal, else prints help and exits 2.

- `pmox init` (the old `pmox configure` prints a rename hint): interactive setup — API URL, token, node SSH credentials, default node/template/storage/bridge, SSH public key; writes `~/.config/pmox/cloud-init/<slug>.yaml`. On a terminal it's one persistent full-page wizard (tabs Connection → Defaults → Access → Review, redrawn in place; network/SSH checks run with an inline spinner and failures stay on their page with answers kept; overwrite / changed-TLS-cert / SSH host-key / enable-snippets questions are in-app dialogs; Esc = back, Ctrl-C = quit, nothing written) ending in a review screen where any answer can be changed before confirming; nothing is written until confirm. Defaults is a single page: node + template/storage/snippet storage/bridge, and changing the node reloads that node's options. Non-interactive/`--no-input`/`--output json` fall back to plain prompts. For the API token you can paste an existing one or choose "generate": pmox logs in with a `user@realm` + password (via `POST /access/ticket`), creates a token with privilege separation off (privsep=0, inherits the user) via `POST /access/users/<user>/token/<name>`, and stores only the token secret — the password is never persisted. Token name is always prompted (default `pmox`); a name collision re-prompts (never overwrites). The URL prompt accepts a bare IP/hostname/`host:port`/web-UI paste (scheme→https, port→8006 filled in, `http`→`https`); it probes reachability before asking for a token and re-asks the address on a network failure (blank/Ctrl-C aborts; non-interactive fails fast). Single-option discovery steps auto-select, except the template step: it always also offers "Build a new Ubuntu template now" alongside any existing templates (even just one), and picking it runs the full `pmox template create` build once node SSH is set up (a few steps later), setting the result as the default; a failed build leaves no default template and warns, it never fails init itself. The SSH-key step offers generate-new-bootstrap-key / use-existing / browse.
- `pmox context list`: print configured server URLs.
- `pmox context delete <url>`: forget a configured server and its keychain secrets.
- `pmox cleanup [--apply]`: reclaim pmox leftovers across all configured contexts in selectable categories — `snippet` (orphaned cloud-init snippets whose VM is gone), `mount-record`/`log`, `cloud-init` (files for removed servers), `tack-profile` (deleted servers/VMs), `secret` (file-backend secrets.yaml for removed servers; OS-keychain not enumerable), `known-host` (stale pins; skipped unless every running VM IP enumerable), `template` (pmox-generated templates `ubuntu-*-pmox-*` in 9000–9099 — DESTRUCTIVE, deletes VMs), `vm` (pmox-tagged VMs missing the `pmox-ready` tag — set once launch/clone completes, right before any post-create hook — so either abandoned mid-launch or still provisioning right now — DESTRUCTIVE, deletes VMs), `context` (a configured server context — same as `pmox context delete`; not cruft, active config — DESTRUCTIVE), and `tack-config` (the whole `~/.config/pmox/tack/` dir, every playbook and role; not cruft, active config — DESTRUCTIVE). Dry-run by default. On a TTY shows a checklist of every category (not just ones with something found — an empty one is listed dimmed as "clean" rather than disappearing; a populated one shows its count and is pre-checked, except the four destructive categories which start unchecked regardless), then asks `Remove N item(s) now? [y/N]` — no need to re-run with `--apply`; declining removes nothing. `--apply` skips the checklist and prompt and removes unconditionally (for scripts/CI). Non-interactive selection via `--only <cats>` / `--skip <cats>` / `--include <cats>` (comma-separated; `--include-templates`/`--include-vms` remain as shorthand for `--include template`/`--include vm`). Aside from opted-in template/vm removal, VMs are never touched. `--output json` supported (never prompts, `--apply` still gates removal there).
- `pmox context list|add|use|current|rename|delete` (`ls`/`rm` aliases): manage contexts; `context add` runs the setup wizard for another server — a context = a configured server addressed by a short name (defaults to its host; `context rename <old> <new>` sets a friendly name). `context use [name]` sets the current context (persisted as `current_context`) so multi-server setups don't need `--context`/`--server` each time — omit the name to pick interactively; `context list` prints a CURRENT/NAME/SERVER table marking the current with `*`; `context current` prints it; `context delete <name>` forgets a context (+secrets, clearing current if it matched).
- `pmox config edit [context]|path|cloud-init [--regenerate]`: `edit` (interactive only) reopens the `pmox init` wizard for an already-configured context landing straight on Review (skips Connection) — the stored token is reused as-is, reachability + the token are re-verified first with nothing re-typed (either failing points at `pmox init`), and jumping back to Defaults/Access pre-fills every field with its current value; `path` prints the config file location; `cloud-init` prints each context's cloud-init template path, `--regenerate` rewrites it.
- `pmox config cloud-init --regenerate`: rewrite the per-server cloud-init file. On a terminal it lets you pick a different SSH key (defaults to the current one) and persists the change to `ssh_pubkey`. Relaunch existing VMs for a new key to apply. Plain `pmox init` also offers to regenerate when a newly-selected key differs from the one in the existing cloud-init file. `pmox doctor` warns on `ssh_pubkey`-vs-cloud-init key drift.
- `pmox template create`: download an Ubuntu cloud image, bake `qemu-guest-agent` in, convert to a template in the 9000–9099 VMID range. Requires PVE 8.0+ and a TTY.
- `pmox launch [name]` (alias `create`): clone the configured template, tag with `pmox`, upload cloud-init snippet, start, wait for guest-agent IP, handshake SSH. On a terminal, a missing name and any of `--cpu`/`--mem`/`--disk` not passed are prompted for (blank reply keeps the built-in default shown in brackets — 2 cores / 2 GiB / 20 GiB); non-interactively (scripts, CI, `--output json`) a missing name is still an error and unset sizing flags still silently use the built-in default, unchanged.
- `pmox vm clone [source] <new-name>`: same state machine as launch, but the source is any existing VM or template. Omit the source to pick it interactively.
- `pmox list`: list pmox-tagged VMs with IPs. `--all` includes every VM on the cluster.
- `pmox info [name|vmid]`: cpu/mem/disk/status/uptime/interfaces for one VM. Arg optional (picker).
- `pmox start [name|vmid]`: start a VM and wait for guest-agent IP. `--no-wait` skips the poll.
- `pmox stop [name|vmid ...]`: ACPI graceful shutdown of one or more VMs. `--force` for hard power-off; `--no-wait` to return as soon as the task is queued. No args → multi-select picker.
- `pmox delete [name|vmid ...]`: stop + destroy + snippet cleanup for one or more VMs. Single confirmation lists all; `--yes` / `PMOX_ASSUME_YES=1` to skip. No args → multi-select picker (space toggles, enter confirms).
- `pmox shell [name|vmid]`: interactive SSH; auto-starts stopped VMs.
- `pmox exec [name|vmid] -- <cmd>`: run one command on a VM over SSH; `--` separator required.
- `pmox apply [name|vmid] [profile]`: run a tack playbook (github.com/tackhq/tack) against a VM, reusing pmox's SSH user/key via `tack run <pb> -c ssh://user@ip --ssh-key <id>`. Auto-starts a stopped VM. Playbook resolution ladder: `--playbook <path>` → profile arg (`~/.config/pmox/tack/<profile>.yaml`) → per-VM remembered profile (state in `~/.local/state/pmox/tack/`) → default `~/.config/pmox/tack/playbook.yaml`. Flags: `--check` (plan only), `-t/--tags`, `--skip-tags`, `-y` (auto-approve; also PMOX_ASSUME_YES / `--output json`), `--ssh-insecure`, `--playbook`, `--init` (scaffold `~/.config/pmox/tack/`; on a terminal, fetches the role list from github.com/tackhq/tack-roles and shows a checklist to pick what to bootstrap with instead of a single hardcoded example role — none selected → a bare starter; non-interactive or fetch failure → same fixed default as always). tack verifies host keys against `~/.ssh/known_hosts` (not pmox's known_hosts_guests); apply and `--tack` both pin an unknown key there themselves before invoking tack (TOFU, same model as guest-VM SSH), skipped by `--ssh-insecure`. tack's subprocess env always sets `TACK_SUDO_NO_PROMPT=1`/`TACK_SSH_NO_PROMPT=1` (every pmox-managed VM has passwordless sudo + key SSH already) so it never blocks on a password prompt. `pmox launch --tack [path]` uses the same invocation (omit path → default playbook). `apply --init <git-url>` clones a playbook repo into ~/.config/pmox/tack (existing dir moved to tack.bak-<ts> after confirmation or -y), discovers playbooks (YAML with a `hosts:` play, roles/ skipped) and sets the default (asks when several; scripts prefer site/playbook/main) — stored as `tack_default_playbook` in config and used by bare `pmox apply <vm>` and `launch --tack`; `apply --default [name]` changes it (picker without a name), `apply --update` git-pulls and re-settles a vanished default; other playbooks run by name: `pmox apply <vm> <name>`.
- `pmox key list` (everyone's published keys: name, fingerprint, published from/when, access). `pmox key publish [--name N] [--context C | --all-contexts] [--replace]` / `unpublish` / `show`: put your SSH PUBLIC key into the cluster's access registry (`/etc/pve/pmox/keys/<name>.pub`, written over node SSH) under your local username, so a cluster admin can grant you VMs. Asks which clusters when several are configured; a different key already under the name needs confirmation (`--replace` non-interactively). Private keys/tokens never leave the machine.
- `pmox access setup` (interactive: People › VMs › Review, full-screen) / `access grant [<vm…>] [--to <name> | --all-vms]` (on a terminal, missing person/VMs are picked interactively) / `access revoke …` / `access show [vm]` (alias `list`) / `access sync [vm…]`: share VMs between people. Desired state in `/etc/pve/pmox/access.yaml` (person → VMIDs or all pmox VMs incl. future); enforced by a `# pmox-access begin/end` block in the guest user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, written via guest-agent file-read/file-write (PVE 9: `VM.GuestAgent.FileRead`+`FileWrite`; PVE 8: `VM.Monitor`; never exec). Lines outside the block are never touched; stopped VMs are pending until `access sync`; launch/clone apply all-VM grants to new VMs (best-effort warning). SSH commands that hit a rejected key print publish/grant/sync guidance and exit 10. `doctor` reports privileges, registry and drift; `cleanup` has `access-grant` (grants for deleted VMs) and opt-in `access-key` (published keys with no grants).
- `pmox vm ssh-config [name|vmid]`: print SSH connection details for a running VM — an OpenSSH config block by default, the full `ssh` command with `--command`, or JSON with `--output json`. Never starts the VM (stopped = error). Arg optional (picker).
- `pmox cp <src> <dst>`: scp-based copy; exactly one side uses `<name>:<path>` (a bare `:path` picks the VM). A missing destination directory is confirmed and created (`--mkdir` without asking).
- `pmox sync <src> <dst>`: rsync-based sync (`rsync -a` by default; `--no-archive` drops it); exactly one side uses `<name>:<path>` (a bare `:path` picks the VM). A missing destination directory is confirmed and created (`--mkdir` without asking).
- `pmox mount <local> [<name>:]<remote>`: watch a local dir and continuously rsync it. Background by default (`--foreground` / `-F` to attach). A missing remote directory is confirmed and created, with sudo when the parent isn't writable (`--mkdir` without asking).
- `pmox umount [<name>:<remote>]`: stop background-mode mounts. With no argument it lists the running mounts to stop (one running mount is stopped without asking; none is success). `--all <vm>` stops every mount for a VM.
- Interactive `<vm>:<path>` target field (mount, cp, sync with missing arguments on a terminal): VM list under the input, greyed default (`<vm>:/mnt/<local dir>` for mount, `<vm>:~/<local dir>` for uploads), Tab completes the VM then remote directories, ↑/↓ picks another VM keeping the path, free editing, Esc back. Exactly one pmox VM is pre-filled and never asked for. Remote paths not starting with `/` or `~/` are relative to the login home. `pmox mount ./src` (local only) asks just for the target.
- `pmox doctor`: readiness check — validates config, API reachability + token privileges (`/access/permissions` diff, names the missing privilege), node online status, storage/template readiness, node SSH, and local tooling. "Ready" means a bare `pmox launch <name>` will actually work: every check that would block it (default node/template/storage/cloud-init, a broken/missing/unmarked template, no guest agent, node SSH unusable) is `fail`, not `warn`. Exits non-zero on any failure using the standard exit-code taxonomy; `--strict` fails on warnings too; `--output json` emits a versioned, per-check-`id` report and never offers a fix. Otherwise, whenever a check carries a known fix (currently: rebuild/convert a broken template, enable the guest agent), doctor offers to run it — confirmed one at a time, or applied without asking via `-y`/`PMOX_ASSUME_YES=1` (works without a TTY) — then automatically re-runs every check and reports the fresh result. `--no-fix` reports only. Without a TTY and without `-y`, nothing is ever offered — a plain, non-interactive run just adds a one-line "N fixable issue(s)" note when relevant. Rebuilding a template reuses `pmox template create`'s own image/storage pickers, so it's only ever offered on a real TTY even under `-y`. `--fix` is accepted but deprecated (a no-op printing a note) — fixes are offered by default now.

## Flags

Persistent root flags (every command):
`--server <name|url>` — target a context by name or server URL (overrides `PMOX_SERVER`).
`--context <name>` — target a context by name (env: `PMOX_CONTEXT`).
Resolution order: `--server` → `--context` → `PMOX_SERVER` → `PMOX_CONTEXT` → current context (`pmox context use`) → single configured → interactive picker.
`--debug` / `-d` — detailed debug output.
`--verbose` / `-v` — verbose progress.
`--no-color` — disable colored output.
`--output <text|json>` — machine-readable output where supported (json implies `--no-input`).
`--no-input` — never prompt; error (exit 2) with the arg to pass instead of showing a picker (env `PMOX_NO_INPUT`). Pickers otherwise appear only when both stdin and stderr are terminals and the identifying arg is omitted; an explicit arg always skips them.
`--ssh-insecure` — skip SSH host-key verification (env `PMOX_SSH_INSECURE`). By default guest-VM SSH (shell/exec/cp/sync/mount) pins host keys on first connect (TOFU) into `~/.config/pmox/known_hosts_guests` and aborts if a pinned key later changes; `--ssh-insecure` disables that.

`pmox launch` / `pmox vm clone`:
`--cpu <cores>`, `--mem <GiB>`, `--disk <GiB>`, `--storage <pool>`, `--snippet-storage <pool>`, `--bridge <name>`, `--node <name>`, `--wait <duration>`, `--no-wait-ssh`, `--post-create <path>`, `--tack <path>`, `--ansible <path>`, `--strict-hooks`.
`--post-create` / `--tack` / `--ansible` are mutually exclusive — one per invocation.

`pmox delete`:
`--yes` / `-y` (skip confirm), `--force` (bypass pmox tag check), `--hard` (hard power-off instead of graceful ACPI shutdown).

`pmox start`:
`--wait <duration>`, `--no-wait`.

`pmox stop`:
`--force`, `--no-wait`.

`pmox shell` / `exec` / `cp` / `sync`:
`--user` / `-u`, `--identity` / `-i`, `--force` (bypass tag check). `cp` adds `--recursive` / `-r`; `cp` and `sync` add `--mkdir`; `sync` adds `--no-archive`.

`pmox vm ssh-config`:
`--user` / `-u`, `--identity` / `-i`, `--force`, `--command` (print an `ssh` command instead of a config block), `--output json`.

`pmox mount`:
`--foreground` / `-F`, `--debounce <duration>`, `--exclude <pattern>` (repeatable), `--no-delete`, `--mkdir`, plus `-- <rsync-extras>`.

`pmox doctor`:
`--strict` (warnings become failures), `--timeout <duration>` (overall budget, default 20s), `--output json` (versioned per-check report, never offers a fix), `--verbose` (list passing checks too), `-y`/`--yes` (apply an offered fix without asking; env `PMOX_ASSUME_YES`), `--no-fix` (report only, never offer a fix), `--fix` (deprecated no-op, kept for compatibility — fixes are offered by default now).

## Exit codes

| Code | Name              | Meaning                                                         |
| ---- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | `ExitOK`          | success                                                         |
| 1    | `ExitGeneric`     | uncategorized error                                             |
| 2    | `ExitUserError`   | invalid user input (bad flag value, prompt refusal)             |
| 3    | `ExitNotFound`    | configured resource missing (server, credential, VM)            |
| 4    | `ExitAPIError`    | PVE API returned a non-2xx other than 401/404                   |
| 5    | `ExitNetworkError`| network or TLS failure reaching the PVE API                     |
| 6    | `ExitUnauthorized`| 401/403 from the PVE API (bad token or missing privilege)       |
| 7    | `ExitTimeout`     | deadline exceeded (wait-IP, wait-SSH, task polling)             |
| 8    | `ExitHook`        | `--strict-hooks` set and a post-create hook failed              |
| 9    | `ExitWarnings`    | `pmox doctor --strict`: all checks passed but warnings present   |

Canonical source: `internal/exitcode/exitcode.go`.

## Config file

Location: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pmox/config.yaml`, else `~/.config/pmox/config.yaml`.
Mode: 0600 file inside a 0700 directory. YAML.

Shape:

```yaml
servers:
  https://pve.lan:8006:
    name: prod           # kubectl-style context name (defaults to host if unset)
    token_id: pmox@pve!pmox
    node: pve
    template: ubuntu-24.04
    storage: local-lvm
    snippet_storage: local
    bridge: vmbr0
    ssh_pubkey: /home/you/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
    user: pmox
    insecure: false      # true = skip TLS verify; pmox then pins the cert (see tls_pin_sha256)
    tls_pin_sha256: ""   # set automatically on first insecure connect; a later mismatch aborts (possible MITM)
    node_ssh:
      user: root
      auth: key          # "password" | "key"
      key_path: /home/you/.ssh/id_ed25519
current_context: prod   # set by 'pmox context use'; targeted when --server/--context/env unset
mount_excludes:
  - .git
  - node_modules
```

Secrets (API token secret, node SSH password, key passphrase) live
in the system keychain via go-keyring — not in `config.yaml`.

Per-server cloud-init user-data:
`~/.config/pmox/cloud-init/<host>-<port>.yaml`. Uploaded as a
`snippets` volume on every launch/clone and referenced via
`cicustom`. Edit in place; `pmox config cloud-init --regenerate`
rewrites it from the stored pubkey.

## Environment variables

- `PMOX_SERVER` — select the target context by name or URL; overridden by `--server`.
- `PMOX_CONTEXT` — select the target context by name; overridden by `--context`.
- `PMOX_SSH_INSECURE` — equivalent to `--ssh-insecure`.
- `PMOX_ASSUME_YES` — equivalent to `--yes` for `pmox delete`.
- `PMOX_NO_INPUT` — equivalent to `--no-input`; disables all interactive pickers/prompts.
- `PMOX_SECRET_STORE` — secret backend selector: `auto` (default; OS keychain if present, else file), `keychain` (error if unavailable), `file` (always `~/.config/pmox/secrets.yaml`, 0600). Secrets never go in `config.yaml`; under `auto` reads try keychain then file, and removal clears both. `pmox doctor` reports the active backend and warns on the plaintext file fallback.
- `PMOX_IP`, `PMOX_VMID`, `PMOX_NAME`, `PMOX_USER`, `PMOX_NODE` — set in the environment of `--post-create` hook scripts.
